results.q: What happens when a monitored node's heartbeat times out?
answer: When a monitored node’s heartbeat times out, `CO_HBconsumer_process()` detects the loss by checking `monitoredNode->timeoutTimer >= monitoredNode->time_us`. It then sets `monitoredNode->NMTstate = CO_NMT_UNKNOWN`, sets `monitoredNode->HBstate = CO_HBconsumer_TIMEOUT`, and calls `CO_error()`. Inside `CO_error()`, if `em == NULL` it returns immediately; otherwise it calculates `uint8_t index = errorBit >> 3` and `uint8_t bitmask = 1U << (errorBit & 0x7U)`.
Losing the data is detected in CO_HBconsumer_process() (301/CO_HBconsumer.c:356), which checks `monitoredNode->timeoutTimer >= monitoredNode->time_us`.

When that happens it sets `monitoredNode->NMTstate = CO_NMT_UNKNOWN`; sets `monitoredNode->HBstate = CO_HBconsumer_TIMEOUT`; calls CO_error() (which checks `em == NULL` (line 640); if true it stops there (returns), sets `uint8_t index = errorBit >> 3` (line 644), sets `uint8_t bitmask = 1U << (errorBit & 0x7U)` (line 645)).

results.q: What happens when a SYNC message has the wrong length?
answer: When a SYNC message has the wrong length, `CO_SYNC_process()` detects the error via `SYNC->receiveError != 0U`, calls `CO_errorReport(SYNC->em, CO_EM_SYNC_LENGTH, CO_EMC_SYNC_DATA_LENGTH, SYNC->receiveError)`, resets `SYNC->receiveError` to 0, and then calls `CO_errorReset(SYNC->em, CO_EM_SYNC_TIME_OUT, 0)`.

Invalid data is caught in CO_SYNC_process() (301/CO_SYNC.c:389): it checks `SYNC->receiveError != 0U`, and when that is true it runs `CO_errorReport(SYNC->em, CO_EM_SYNC_LENGTH, CO_EMC_SYNC_DATA_LENGTH, SYNC->receiveError)` and records it (`SYNC->receiveError = 0`).
When it does not return there, CO_SYNC_process() goes on to call CO_error() with (`CO_errorReset(SYNC->em, CO_EM_SYNC_TIME_OUT, 0)`) (line 403).

CO_error() checks `em == NULL` (line 640); if true it stops there (returns); then it sets `uint8_t index = errorBit >> 3` (line 644); then it sets `uint8_t bitmask = 1U << (errorBit & 0x7U)` (line 645); then it checks `index >= (CO_CONFIG_EM_ERR_STATUS_BITS_COUNT / 8U)` (line 648); if true it sets `index = CO_EM_WRONG_ERROR_REPORT >> 3`, `bitmask = 1U << (CO_EM_WRONG_ERROR_REPORT & 0x7U)`; then it sets `uint8_t* errorStatusBits = &em->errorStatusBits[index]` (line 655); then it sets `uint8_t errorStatusBitMasked = *errorStatusBits & bitmask` (line 656).

Consequence: OD_read_1003() checks `stream->subIndex <= em->fifoCount` (301/CO_Emergency.c:175); `stream->subIndex <= em->fifoCount` depends on runtime values, so it may return early and may call CO_setUint32().

Consequence: CO_EM_process() checks `(!em->CANtxBuff->bufferFull) && (fifoPpPtr != em->fifoWrPtr)` (301/CO_Emergency.c:575); `(!em->CANtxBuff->bufferFull) && (fifoPpPtr != em->fifoWrPtr)` depends on runtime values, so it may call memcpy() and may call CO_CANsend() and may run `CO_errorReport(em, CO_EM_EMERGENCY_BUFFER_FULL, CO_EMC_GENERIC, 0)` and may run `CO_errorReset(em, CO_EM_EMERGENCY_BUFFER_FULL, 0)`.

Consequence: CO_EM_process() checks `em->fifoOverflow == 1U` (301/CO_Emergency.c:598); with em.fifoOverflow = 1, fifoOverflow = 1, `em->fifoOverflow == 1U` is true, so it runs `CO_errorReport(em, CO_EM_EMERGENCY_BUFFER_FULL, CO_EMC_GENERIC, 0)`.

Bad input is also rejected in other places: CO_SYNC_init() rejects it when `(OD_1007_syncWindowLen != NULL) && (SYNC->OD_1007_window == NULL)` (301/CO_SYNC.c:232), reporting `*errInfo = OD_getIndex(OD_1007_syncWindowLen)`; CO_TPDOsend() rejects it when `(verifyLength > CO_PDO_MAX_SIZE) || (verifyLength != (OD_size_t)PDO->dataLength)` (301/CO_PDO.c:1324); CO_storageEeprom_init() rejects it when `(entry->addr == NULL) || (entry->len == 0U) || (entry->subIndexOD < 2U)` (storage/CO_storageEeprom.c:129), reporting `*storageInitError = i`.

results.q: What happens when the CAN controller goes bus-off?
answer: When the CAN controller goes bus‑off, `CO_EM_process()` detects the `CO_CAN_ERRTX_BUS_OFF` flag and calls `CO_error()` with `CO_EM_CAN_TX_BUS_OFF` and `CO_EMC_BUS_OFF_RECOVERED`. After that, the function continues to check other error bits and may send emergency messages via `CO_CANsend()`. The exact subsequent actions depend on runtime values such as `em->fifoCount`, `em->fifoWrPtr`, and `em->fifoOverflow`.

This is handled in CO_EM_process() (301/CO_Emergency.c:507): it checks `(CANerrStChanged & CO_CAN_ERRTX_BUS_OFF) != 0U`, and when that is true it calls CO_error(em, (CANerrSt & CO_CAN_ERRTX_BUS_OFF) != 0U, CO_EM_CAN_TX_BUS_OFF, CO_EMC_BUS_OFF_RECOVERED, 0).

When it does not return there, CO_EM_process() goes on to call CO_error() with (`em`, `(CANerrSt & CO_CAN_ERRTX_OVERFLOW) != 0U`, `CO_EM_CAN_TX_OVERFLOW`) (line 511); CO_error() with (`em`, `(CANerrSt & CO_CAN_ERRTX_PDO_LATE) != 0U`, `CO_EM_TPDO_OUTSIDE_WINDOW`) (line 514); CO_error() with (`em`, `(CANerrSt & CO_CAN_ERRRX_PASSIVE) != 0U`, `CO_EM_CAN_RX_BUS_PASSIVE`) (line 517); CO_error() with (`em`, `(CANerrSt & CO_CAN_ERRRX_OVERFLOW) != 0U`, `CO_EM_CAN_RXB_OVERFLOW`) (line 520); CO_CANsend() with (`em->CANdevTx`, `em->CANtxBuff`) (line 582).

CO_error() checks `em == NULL` (line 640); if true it stops there (returns); then it sets `uint8_t index = errorBit >> 3` (line 644); then it sets `uint8_t bitmask = 1U << (errorBit & 0x7U)` (line 645); then it checks `index >= (CO_CONFIG_EM_ERR_STATUS_BITS_COUNT / 8U)` (line 648); if true it sets `index = CO_EM_WRONG_ERROR_REPORT >> 3`, `bitmask = 1U << (CO_EM_WRONG_ERROR_REPORT & 0x7U)`; then it sets `uint8_t* errorStatusBits = &em->errorStatusBits[index]` (line 655); then it sets `uint8_t errorStatusBitMasked = *errorStatusBits & bitmask` (line 656).

Consequence: OD_read_1003() checks `stream->subIndex <= em->fifoCount` (301/CO_Emergency.c:175); `stream->subIndex <= em->fifoCount` depends on runtime values, so it may return early and may call CO_setUint32().

Consequence: CO_EM_process() checks `(!em->CANtxBuff->bufferFull) && (fifoPpPtr != em->fifoWrPtr)` (301/CO_Emergency.c:575); `(!em->CANtxBuff->bufferFull) && (fifoPpPtr != em->fifoWrPtr)` depends on runtime values, so it may call memcpy() and may call CO_CANsend() and may run `CO_errorReport(em, CO_EM_EMERGENCY_BUFFER_FULL, CO_EMC_GENERIC, 0)` and may run `CO_errorReset(em, CO_EM_EMERGENCY_BUFFER_FULL, 0)`.

Consequence: CO_EM_process() checks `em->fifoOverflow == 1U` (301/CO_Emergency.c:598); with em.fifoOverflow = 1, fifoOverflow = 1, `em->fifoOverflow == 1U` is true, so it runs `CO_errorReport(em, CO_EM_EMERGENCY_BUFFER_FULL, CO_EMC_GENERIC, 0)`.
The function that computes the CRC is `crc16_ccitt()`.

The default configuration of this code leaves it out, so the answer below describes a build with those features switched on.
It is computed in crc16_ccitt():
crc16_ccitt() (301/crc16-ccitt.c:71) — Calculate CRC sum on block of data.
Step by step, it repeats while `i < blockLength` (line 75); then it sets `uint8_t tmp = (uint8_t)((uint8_t)(crc >> 8U) ^ block[i])` (line 76); then it returns `crc` (line 79).

answer: The NMT operating state is set in `CO_NMT_init()` (CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:95‑96) where `NMT->operatingState = CO_NMT_INITIALIZING` and `NMT->operatingStatePrev = CO_NMT_INITIALIZING` are assigned. It is set in CO_NMT_init():
CO_NMT_init() (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:72) — Initialize NMT and Heartbeat producer object.

Step by step, it sets `CO_ReturnError_t ret = CO_ERROR_NO` (line 79); then it checks `(NMT == NULL) || (OD_1017_ProducerHbTime == NULL) || (em == NULL) || (NMT_CANdevRx == NULL) || (HB_CANdevTx == NULL)` (line 82); if true it returns `CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT` straight away; then it calls memset(NMT, 0, sizeof(CO_NMT_t)) (line 92); then it updates NMT (operatingState, operatingStatePrev, nodeId, NMTcontrol, em, HBproducerTimer; lines 95–100); then it calls OD_get_u16(OD_1017_ProducerHbTime, 0, &HBprodTime_ms, true) and stores the result in `odRet` (line 104); then it checks `odRet != ODR_OK` (ODR_OK = 0) (line 105); if true it returns `CO_ERROR_OD_PARAMETERS` straight away; then it checks `errInfo != NULL` (line 106); if true it calls OD_getIndex() and sets `*errInfo = OD_getIndex(OD_1017_ProducerHbTime)`; then it sets `NMT->HBproducerTime_us = (uint32_t)HBprodTime_ms * 1000U` (line 111); then it sets `NMT->OD_1017_extension.object = NMT` (line 113); then it sets `NMT->OD_1017_extension.read = OD_readOriginal` (line 114); ….

The update itself: `NMT->operatingState = CO_NMT_INITIALIZING` (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:95); `NMT->operatingStatePrev = CO_NMT_INITIALIZING` (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:96); `NMT->NMTcontrol = NMTcontrol` (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:98).
The result is stored in CO_CANopenInit.err by CO_CANopenInit() (CANopen.c:1040: `err = CO_NMT_init(co->NMT, OD_GET(H1017, OD_H1017_PRODUCER_HB_TIME), em, nodeId, NMTcontrol, firstHBTime_ms,`).

Related values are also set here: `NMT->operatingState = NMTstateCpy` in CO_NMT_process() (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:264); `NMT->operatingStatePrev = NMTstateCpy` in CO_NMT_process() (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:205); `monitoredNode->NMTstate = CO_NMT_UNKNOWN` in CO_HBconsumer_initEntry() (301/CO_HBconsumer.c:194); `HBconsNode->NMTstate = (CO_NMT_internalState_t)data[0]` in CO_HBcons_receive() (301/CO_HBconsumer.c:45); `monitoredNode->NMTstate = CO_NMT_UNKNOWN` in CO_HBconsumer_process() (301/CO_HBconsumer.c:365); `monitoredNode->NMTstate = CO_NMT_UNKNOWN` in CO_HBconsumer_process() (301/CO_HBconsumer.c:408).

The value is computed just before: `NMTstateCpy = CO_NMT_OPERATIONAL` (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:239); `NMTstateCpy = (((uint16_t)NMT->NMTcontrol & (uint16_t)CO_NMT_STARTUP_TO_OPERATIONAL) != 0U) ? CO_NMT_OPERATIONAL : CO_NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL` (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:195); `const uint8_t* data = CO_CANrxMsg_readData(msg)` (301/CO_HBconsumer.c:41).

results.q: When is the heartbeat message sent?
answer: The heartbeat is sent by `CO_NMT_process()` when the condition `NNTinit || ((NMT->HBproducerTime_us != 0U) && ((NMT->HBproducerTimer == 0U) || (NMTstateCpy != NMT->operatingStatePrev)))` is true, and `CO_NMT_process()` itself is called by `CO_process()` only if `co->nodeIdUnconfigured` is false and `CO_GET_CNT(NMT) == 1U`. The call chain starts from `main()` → `CO_process()` → `CO_NMT_process()`.

CO_NMT_process() does it with `(void)CO_CANsend(NMT->HB_CANdevTx, NMT->HB_TXbuff)` (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:191), only when `NNTinit || ((NMT->HBproducerTime_us != 0U) && ((NMT->HBproducerTimer == 0U) || (NMTstateCpy != NMT->operatingStatePrev)))` is true.

CO_NMT_process() itself: It is called by CO_process() at CANopen.c:1368 with (`co->NMT`, `&NMTstate`, `timeDifference_us`, `timerNext_us`), only when `co->nodeIdUnconfigured` is false, only when `CO_GET_CNT(NMT) == 1U` is true. The full chain from the program's start is: main() → CO_process() → CO_NMT_process().

results.q: What happens to the NMT state when an error occurs while the node is operational?
answer: When an error occurs while the node is operational, `CO_NMT_process()` sets `NMTstateCpy` to `CO_NMT_STOPPED` if the control bit `CO_NMT_ERR_TO_STOPPED` is set, otherwise it sets it to `CO_NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL`. Then, if the control bit `CO_NMT_ERR_FREE_TO_OPERATIONAL` is set, the state is changed back to `CO_NMT_OPERATIONAL` only if `NMTstateCpy` is `CO_NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL` and neither `busOff_HB` nor `errRegMasked` are true.

Invalid data is caught in CO_NMT_process() (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:234): it checks `(NMTstateCpy == CO_NMT_OPERATIONAL) && (busOff_HB || errRegMasked)`, and when that is true it sets `NMTstateCpy = (((uint16_t)NMT->NMTcontrol & (uint16_t)CO_NMT_ERR_TO_STOPPED) != 0U) ? CO_NMT_STOPPED : CO_NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL` (CO_NMT_STOPPED = 4, CO_NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL = 127) (line 235); then it checks `(((uint16_t)NMT->NMTcontrol & (uint16_t)CO_NMT_ERR_FREE_TO_OPERATIONAL) != 0U) && (NMTstateCpy == CO_NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL) && (!busOff_HB && !errRegMasked)` (CO_NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL = 127) (line 237).

results.q: What happens when an SDO client requests an object that does not exist?
answer: When an SDO client requests a non‑existent object, `OD_getSub()` returns `ODR_IDX_NOT_EXIST`. The caller then propagates this error up the call chain, ultimately causing `CO_SDOserver_process()` to return the error code via `OD_getSDOabCode()`.

This is handled in OD_getSub() (301/CO_ODinterface.c:182): it checks `(entry == NULL) || (entry->odObject == NULL)`, and when that is true it returns `ODR_IDX_NOT_EXIST`, so the rest of OD_getSub() is skipped.
OD_getSub()'s caller OD_get_value() checks `ret != ODR_OK` (301/CO_ODinterface.c:321) and then returns `ret`.
OD_getSub()'s caller OD_set_value() checks `ret != ODR_OK` (301/CO_ODinterface.c:343) and then returns `ret`.
OD_getSub()'s caller PDOconfigMap() checks `odRet != ODR_OK` (301/CO_PDO.c:115) and then returns `odRet`.
PDOconfigMap()'s caller PDO_initMapping() checks `odRet != ODR_OK` (301/CO_PDO.c:200) and then reports `*erroneousMap = map` to its caller.
PDOconfigMap()'s caller OD_write_PDO_mapping() checks `odRet != ODR_OK` (301/CO_PDO.c:294) and then returns `odRet`.
OD_getSub()'s caller CO_SDOserver_process() checks `odRet != ODR_OK` (301/CO_SDOserver.c:645) and then calls OD_getSDOabCode().

Step by step, it checks `(fifo == NULL) || (fifo->buf == NULL) || (buf == NULL)` (line 83); if true it returns `0` straight away; then it sets `bufDest = &fifo->buf[fifo->writePtr]` (line 87); then it repeats while `i > 0U` (line 88); then it sets `size_t writePtrNext = fifo->writePtr + 1U` (line 89); then it checks `(writePtrNext == fifo->readPtr) || ((writePtrNext == fifo->bufSize) && (fifo->readPtr == 0U))` (line 92); if true it leaves the loop (`break`); then it checks `crc != NULL` (line 99); if true it calls crc16_ccitt_single(); then it checks `writePtrNext == fifo->bufSize` (line 105); if true it sets `fifo->writePtr = 0`, `bufDest = &fifo->buf[0]`; otherwise it sets `fifo->writePtr++`; then it returns `count - i` (line 115).

results.q: Where does the data in CANrxData come from?
answer: `CANrxData` is filled by the functions `CO_PDO_receive()` and `CO_SDO_receive()`.
